items.question: What is Better Resource Monitor?
items.answer: A free, open-source menu bar app that shows CPU, memory, storage, GPU, and network usage on macOS. Written in Rust. Under 0.1% CPU and about 15 MB of RAM.

items.question: Who is Better Resource Monitor for?
items.answer: It is for Mac users who want a lightweight, always-visible menu bar view of CPU, memory, storage, GPU, and network usage without admin prompts or telemetry. It works on Intel and Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 13 or newer.

items.question: Who should choose a deeper system monitor instead?
items.answer: Choose Stats or iStat Menus if you need fan, temperature, battery, detailed sensor history, or broader hardware controls. Better Resource Monitor intentionally focuses on the core daily metrics.

items.question: Which macOS versions are supported?
items.answer: It works on Intel Macs and Apple Silicon Macs running macOS Ventura 13 or newer.

items.question: Is it free?
items.answer: Yes. Both distributions are free, MIT-licensed, and include the same monitoring features. The Mac App Store handles updates automatically; GitHub downloads are updated manually.

items.question: How much CPU and memory does it use?
items.answer: Under 0.1% CPU and about 15 MB of RAM on an Apple M1. For comparison, Stats uses ~50 MB and iStat Menus uses 100+ MB. The app binary is under 7 MB.

items.question: How does GPU monitoring work?
items.answer: On macOS, it reads device utilization from Apple Silicon GPUs through Apple's public IOAccelerator API. That keeps GPU monitoring available in both the App Store and GitHub versions without relying on private APIs or sudo.

items.question: Does it collect any data?
items.answer: No. Zero network requests, no analytics, no telemetry. Everything stays on your machine. Storage usage comes from OS-reported total/free capacity for the selected local volume, defaulting to the volume containing your home folder. The disk picker reads local volume names, mount points, and capacity, including external disks; it does not read file names or contents. The source code is on GitHub if you want to verify that yourself.

items.question: Is Better Resource Monitor a Stats or iStat Menus alternative?
items.answer: Yes, if you want a simpler macOS menu bar monitor focused on CPU, memory, storage, GPU, and network usage. Stats and iStat Menus go deeper into sensors; Eul was a similar lightweight option that is no longer actively maintained. Better Resource Monitor stays lighter, free, and fully available from the Mac App Store. See all [comparisons]({{comparisonUrl}}), or jump to [Stats]({{vsStatsUrl}}), [iStat Menus]({{vsIstatMenusUrl}}), or [Eul]({{vsEulUrl}}).

items.question: Does it drain MacBook battery?
items.answer: It is designed for low overhead, but battery impact depends on your Mac and workload. It reads macOS thermal status through public APIs; it does not report individual sensor temperatures or fan speeds.

items.question: Is Better Resource Monitor a macOS Activity Monitor alternative?
items.answer: It is an always-visible menu bar companion for quick glances at CPU, memory, storage, GPU, and network usage. It does not replace Activity Monitor's detailed process list or full-window tools; open Activity Monitor when you need to inspect or manage individual processes.
